sources.quote: connected Berkenbush to a network of at least 10 of these 527 groups that have raised more than $33 million on the promise of supporting admirable causes
sources.searcher_note: Names 10 police/fire/veteran/cancer 527s (National Committee for Volunteer Firefighters, National Coalition for Disabled Veterans PAC, National Police & Sheriffs Coalition PAC, American Breast Cancer Coalition, National Cancer Alliance, etc.); about 90 cents of each dollar goes to fundraising; ABCC spent under half of 1% on 'voter advocacy.'

sources.quote: ProPublica found a network of 527s that purport to support police, veterans, cancer patients and firefighters, but appear to largely be spending their donation money on a small group of fundraisers and administrative companies that support more fundraising efforts.
sources.searcher_note: Launch of ProPublica's 527 Explorer, built on IRS 8872 filings; same finding as the lead at category level.

sources.quote: But just spent 1 percent of the money they raised to help candidates via donations, ads or targeted get out the votes messages
sources.searcher_note: Quotes the New York Times front page of May 2023 ('Tugging Hearts to Raise $89 Million, but Sending A Scant 1% to the Causes') on police/veteran/firefighter 527s. Earliest same-finding coverage found at the 1%-to-candidates level; names no groups.

sources.quote: In the space of two years, ABCC has brought in nearly $3.57 million, according to IRS filings
sources.searcher_note: American Breast Cancer Coalition, a cancer-named 527, paid nearly every dollar raised to fundraising companies. Earliest 527-specific coverage found.

sources.quote: have raised more than $140 million in the last two election cycles alone
sources.searcher_note: Pattern for the lead's look-alike FEC PACs: 43 police/veteran/firefighter/cancer-named FEC PACs on one call center's client list; not the 527s.

notes: The frozen lead doesn't list its 19 groups, so I can't confirm which groups the sources overlap with. Sources name police/fire/veteran/cancer 527s (ProPublica's 10 groups, the NYT's five linked groups via Give.org, ABCC) and report the same finding: most money goes to fundraisers, about 1% or less to candidates. No source found has the lead's $193.7M total, the 19-group count, the $0.36M in contributions, the 58% fundraising/caging share, or the donor overlap with 13 FEC PACs. The New York Times original (nytimes.com/interactive/2023/05/14/us/politics/scam-robocalls-donations-policing-veterans.html, May 14, 2023: five linked groups, $89M since 2014, 1% to candidates) couldn't be fetched, so it isn't recorded; the Seattle Times reprint returned 403, as did OpenSecrets' Oct 2021 piece. Nothing found dated after 2026-06-30. The FTC/AG query found only charity-fraud actions, none against these 527s.
